newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech airline CSA carries 1.7 mln passengers in 96.
newsitem.headline: Czech airline CSA carries 1.7 mln passengers in 96.

text.p: Czech airline Ceska Aerolinie a.s. (CSA) said the number of passengers it carried in 1996 rose 12 percent, year-on-year, to 1.68 million, the CTK news agency reported on Friday.

CTK quoted CSA Marketing Director Jiri Prusa, who was speaking at a travel symposium in the city of Brno, as saying that despite rising revenues, mounting fuel costs have forced the airline to raise its ticket prices.
The airline raised ticket prices through an extra charge on January 1 by an average of three percent to offset higher fuel costs.
CSA posted a preliminary first-half loss, according to Czech accounting standards, of 180 million crowns ($6.7 million), down 25 percent from the first half of 1995.

CSA is majority-owned by the state through its agencies Konsolidcani Banka a.s. and the National Property Fund, a state privatisation agency. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (ERBD) holds a 16 percent share of CSA.
Other minor shareholders include the investment fund RIF and insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s..
